reviewed_scope: Nintendo handheld and home-console title-specific decompilation, recompilation, reimplementation, and native-port repositories discovered through GitHub searches and community/tracker leads. Maintainer repositories, README/build documentation, and releases were used to verify included claims. Similar-title records in the catalog are retained as separate entries only where the source identifies a distinct project, version, or host target.

projects.title: Dragon Quest IX European Native Recompilation Research
projects.game: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies (European release)
projects.platform: Nintendo DS Europe → Linux desktop; Windows and Steam Deck are listed as targets without validation
projects.status: Research-stage tooling and runtime are published, but the README says no end-to-end game generator or playable build is available. It reports aggregate matching figures from a local run while noting that full-module verification and runtime parity remain incomplete.
projects.summary: Title-specific ARM9/ARM7 static-recompilation tooling and an experimental Nintendo DS runtime for Dragon Quest IX's European release. The repository contains no generated game code or game data.
projects.strategy: Static recompilation of ARM9/ARM7 code to native C++; experimental SDL2 and Godot hosts
projects.source_available: Public research tooling and runtime; requires a user-supplied European game copy. The README says title-specific generated code and an end-to-end generation workflow are not published.
projects.subtype: European Nintendo DS release; native runtime parity and Windows/Steam Deck validation are not established

sources.label: Maintainer README: target, method, status, inputs, and limitations

projects.title: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days Native PC Port
projects.platform: Nintendo DS → Windows, Linux, and macOS
projects.status: Early development. The front end runs natively through character select and an experimental Twilight Town gameplay harness is available; the README says the game does not yet have a reconstructed mission or combat loop.
projects.summary: A native C++ PC source port that adapts understood game code and behavior to a portable runtime. Its maintainer explicitly separates it from the project's matching Nintendo DS decompilation.
projects.strategy: Native source port with a portable PC runtime, rendering, input, audio, and filesystem support
projects.source_available: Public source repository; users must provide their own game copy. The repository says it contains no ROM, game assets, or copyrighted binaries.
projects.subtype: PC port; supported game region/revision is not specified in the reviewed README

sources.label: Maintainer README: project relationship, supported hosts, status, and game-file requirement

projects.title: Air Traffic Chaos Nintendo DS Decompilation
projects.status: Early work in progress. The README documents extraction, configuration, and ROM rebuild commands, but does not report matching progress or claim a complete decompilation.
projects.summary: A Nintendo DS decompilation and modification project with ARM9 reverse-engineering sources and a documented rebuild-and-diff workflow for the USA ROM.
projects.strategy: Nintendo DS ROM extraction/rebuild using dsd plus reverse-engineered C; byte-matching status is not stated
projects.source_available: Public source repository; the README instructs users to provide the USA game ROM and a DS BIOS7 dump. No release is listed.
projects.subtype: USA release; ROM identity is supplied by the project README

projects.title: BIT.TRIP COMPLETE Wii Decompilation
projects.platform: Nintendo Wii (Game ID SVTEXS; region not specified in the README)

projects.summary: A Wii decompilation of the BIT.TRIP COMPLETE compilation. The maintainer says the same repository also covers the individual BIT.TRIP WiiWare entries in effect; this batch records the compilation once because separate entry build targets are not enumerated in the README.
projects.strategy: DTK-based source decompilation; matching status is not stated
projects.source_available: Public source repository; a user-supplied Wii disc image with Game ID SVTEXS is required to configure and build. The README says game assets and assembly are not included.

projects.title: The Sims: Bustin' Out GameCube Decompilation
projects.status: Work in progress. The README reports 6.24% whole-executable matching, with 11.43% of game-code functions matched at the time of its status table.
projects.summary: A matching GameCube decompilation targeting USA revision 0. It aims to rebuild an executable byte-identical to the disc using the original SN Systems ProDG toolchain; game assets and disc code are not included.
projects.strategy: Matching C/C++ decompilation using SN Systems ProDG for GameCube
projects.source_available: Public source repository; requires a user-supplied GameCube copy. The README identifies the target main.dol SHA-1 as 26f0bf319a5fd3ea3d3d86e6117fbc78e259231c.
projects.subtype: USA G4ME69 revision 0; original CodeWarrior is not the target toolchain

projects.status: Playable through Viridian City according to the README; not completed from start to finish. Only the Eevee v1.0.0 release on Windows is documented as supported.

review_notes.note: The maintainer README describes BIT.TRIP COMPLETE for Wii and says the repository effectively covers each individual WiiWare entry. It gives one disc Game ID (SVTEXS) and one build workflow but does not enumerate distinct per-entry build targets, so one compilation-level record is staged and no per-entry rows are inferred.

GitHub searches were supplemented with Reddit searches, including the Super Robot Wars 64 project announcement. The decomp.dev homepage currently reports that its public index and new project additions are disabled, so it was used as tracker context rather than evidence for project claims. Community and tracker results were checked against maintainer repositories/readmes/releases before inclusion.

The README remains the generic DTK template, but the repository has game-specific SAUJ8P configuration and substantial title-specific symbol/split maps. It is included as an early, unverified scaffold with no claim of built or matched game code.
